title: Add cohort-aware spiral prober and rollback curator for transient regression isolation
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: We repeatedly see short-lived latency spikes that trigger standard canaries and cause unnecessary rollbacks. This PR implements a cohort-aware probing strategy ("spiral prober") plus a lightweight rollback curator that isolates transient regressions from persistent degradations and provides a staged rollback budget for safe cutovers. The change is intended to reduce noise-driven rollbacks while preserving sensitivity to real regressions.
commits_summary: 5 commits: 1) implement spiral prober algorithm and scheduler + unit tests; 2) integrate prober into canary-orchestrator and add cohort tagging; 3) rollback curator policy engine with quarantine credits and staged rollback budgets; 4) add observability: new metrics, dashboards, tracing hooks, and e2e perf harness; 5) docs, config schema, and docs fixes; plus a follow-up commit to fix a probe scheduler race under high throughput.

release_notes: Adds a cohort-aware spiral prober that samples traffic in spiraling temporal windows to distinguish transient spikes from sustained regressions. Introduces a rollback curator with quarantine credits, staged rollback budgets, and configurable sensitivity knobs. Default configuration: disabled for existing canaries; opt-in via canary.policy.prober.enabled=true. Observability: new metrics (canary.spiral.probes_total, canary.spiral.detected_transients, curator.rollback_credits), dashboards and traces included.
rationale: Existing canaries trigger too eagerly on short-lived tail spikes; this approach prioritizes cohort diversity and temporal spiral sampling to improve signal-to-noise. The rollback curator provides a conservative staged rollback mechanism to avoid oscillation during noisy traffic patterns while still enabling rapid remediation for persistent problems.
notes_on_risks_and_mitigation: Risk: misconfigured sensitivity could delay detection of real regressions. Mitigation: feature is opt-in, sensitivity defaults to conservative values, and the rollback curator emits detailed telemetry and runbooks. Added a safety gate in orchestrator that prevents rollbacks exceeding the staged budget and an emergency override route for SRE.
usage_examples: 1) Enable on a canary: PATCH /canaries/:id { "policy": { "prober": { "type": "spiral", "enabled": true, "sensitivity": "conservative" } } } 2) Inspector: metrics can be queried via PromQL: sum(rate(canary_spiral_detected_transients[5m])) by (canary, cohort). 3) Rollback curator status: GET /canaries/:id/curator -> returns credits, quarantined cohorts, staged_budget.
post_merge_actions: 1) Schedule a 2-week canary on low-traffic services to validate tuning; 2) Add a short runbook for SRE explaining curator metrics and emergency override; 3) Follow-up PR to add sampling visualization in Console (ENG-3470).
back_compat: No breaking API changes. New config keys are optional and default to disabled for existing canaries.
qa_summary: Unit tests added for core prober logic and curator policy, integration tests for orchestrator interactions, and perf-e2e harness validated that noise-driven rollbacks dropped by ~60% in a synthetic burst workload. QA notes: one flaky test fixed by adjusting scheduler timeouts; no production incidents observed during staged rollout on canary fleet.
notes_for_oncall: If oncall observes sustained regressions while this prober is enabled, check curator.rollback_credits and canary.spiral.detected_transients to determine if incidents are transient or persistent. Emergency override endpoint documented in SRE runbook.
